pr_title: Integrate CCS with new search_shards API
pr_body:
This PR integrates CCS with the new search_shards API. With this change, we will be able to skip shards on the coordinator on remote clusters using the timestamps stored in the cluster state.

Relates #94534
Closes #93730

issue_context.title: Search shards API to rewrite query and skip shards
issue_context.body:
The search shards API is a public API, that the search and async search API use internally when executing cross-cluster search requests (and roundtrips are not minimized). For each remote cluster involved in the search request, search shards will be invoked to collect information about the remote shards that have to be queried. The API accepts a set of indices and returns a set of shards that the coordinating node includes in the search request.  Ideally, such API would accept a query and perform the coordinator can_match phase, so that it does not return shards that could be easily skipped. The coordinator can_match phase skips shards based on index metadata (min and max) that is present in the cluster state, which the CCS coordinating cluster is not aware of for remote indices.

This would help unify the search behaviour between local and remote searches. Today searchable snapshots allow to skip shards completely when the query has a timerange filter against the `@timestamp` field that can not possibly match, and this is good to avoid throwing shards failures for irrelevant shards in the situation where frozen indices are not available (can happen as they don't have replicas).
comments:
> Ideally, such API would accept a query and perform the coordinator can_match phase

I think it should perform the _whole_ `can_match` phase, both the coordinator-side work based on index metadata and the data-node-side work based on query rewriting.

I find that surprising, I view search shards as a coordinator action, as it does not go to the data nodes. This would change the search shards API execution significantly. Also, we would need to account for remote shards that already executed can_match as part of the ordinary search execution, which sounds like it would introduce complexity. On the other hand, it would minimize the number of shard level requests from the coordinating node to the remote shards to (dfs +)  query + fetch. Is that the goal you are looking to achieve or is there more to it?

I think that's about it. The coordinator-side can-match phase is very weak, since it only looks at timestamp range queries on a field called `@timestamp`. The full can-match phase handles all timestamp ranges and `constant_keyword` fields, and may extend to more rewrites in future.

When we reach out to a remote cluster to get a list of shards for the subsequent phases of the search, it seems a bit odd to me not to try and reduce the length of that list as far as possible within the remote cluster before responding.
I see that #94534 has an 8.8 tag and was curios if the changes to CCS to use the new API would be coming in 8.8 as well or likely slated for 8.9 or later?

@wrathagom we can't guarantee that the full set of changes will make it into 8.8. #94534 focuses on the downstream clusters, and we will have to then make adjustments to the coordinating side of the execution.

review_comments:
A minor nice-to-have, but it would be good to move the javadoc from the other constructor down to this one and document the new parameters.

I had to go down to the "getter" methods for `skip` and `prefiltered` to understand what they represented.

Now that I see search shards being used, I am wondering why we need two flags in `SearchShardsResponse`. Intuitively, anything returned from that API is prefiltered by definition, and do we need the list of skipped shards or could we replace that with a counter? Maybe we need a third class for the bw compatibility layer that incorporates the SearchShardsGroup and tell where it comes from (old or new). It looks to me like serializing these flags over the wire is not necessary, is that the case?

I know this is controversial, but the BWC layer is very small. I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/96123 to remove the `prefilter` flag. I will try to come up with an  alternative here.

@javanna I have pushed https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/95894/commits/8f5b715aaeac886f0d4f1551141ea5b0d067921b to handle the `preFiltered` flag. I think this approach is cleaner. WDYT? Thank you for pushing it.
Do we need this because it is difficult to test directly against searchable snapshots, which is the only case where we rewrite on the coord node?

I find this test useful, at the same time I wish that we could split it and test different aspects separately. I wish that certain parts could be tested via unit test as well.

Some aspects that seem important to test (including those that relate to the previous PR around adding the search shards API):
- search shards excludes shards that cannot match based on metadata from the cluster state (frozen indices only)
-  search shards returns only shards that may match based on the can match executed on the data nodes
- shards that are returned don't execute can match once again as part of the can match for local shards, while we do execute can match for the other shards
- the number of skipped shards reflects the total number of skipped shards across all clusters

I believe an IT test here is more suitable because we are performing a real CCS search and assert our expectation. I've hardened this test (in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/95894/commits/0409f7300bb774fb1cbe7dce452611e2d32161d0) to cover all the bullets.

minor nitpick:

The string `"cluster_a"` is repeated several times throughout the class. Would it be better to create a static final String called REMOTE_CLUSTER, so as to not repeat and also make code like this look more uniform:

```
for (String cluster : List.of(LOCAL_CLUSTER, REMOTE_CLUSTER)) {
```

instead of 

```
for (String cluster : List.of(LOCAL_CLUSTER, "cluster_a")) {
```
